subject: math
title: The Pythagorean Theorem: Squares on the Sides, the Hypotenuse and Missing Legs
seo_title: Grade 8 Pythagorean Theorem Worksheets: Find the Hypotenuse and a Missing Side (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Describe the Pythagorean relationship using various geometric models, and apply the theorem to solve problems involving an unknown side length for a given right triangle
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 math worksheets on the Pythagorean theorem for the Ontario curriculum: the area model with squares on the sides, identifying the hypotenuse, finding the hypotenuse or a missing leg (rounded to the nearest tenth), and word problems with ladders, ramps, parks and TV screens. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_sub: In a right triangle, the square on the hypotenuse c (the side opposite the right angle) equals the squares on the two legs added together. To find the hypotenuse, add the squares and take the square root. To find a leg, subtract the squares and take the square root.
body_html:
Legs and hypotenuse

A right triangle has one 90° angle, shown with a small square. The two sides that form the right angle are the legs (a and b). The side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse (c). It is always the longest side, and it can point in any direction.

The area model: a² + b² = c²

Draw a square on each side of a right triangle. The two squares on the legs together have exactly the same area as the square on the hypotenuse. This is the Pythagorean theorem.

It only works for right triangles. It also works the other way: if a² + b² = c², the triangle has a right angle.

Find the hypotenuse: add the squares

Square the two legs, add, then take the square root.

Example

The legs are 6 cm and 8 cm. Find the hypotenuse.

c² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100. c = √100 = 10.

Answer: 10 cm

Round at the end

The legs are 4 cm and 7 cm. Find the hypotenuse to the nearest tenth.

c² = 16 + 49 = 65. c = √65 ≈ 8.06, which rounds to 8.1.

Answer: 8.1 cm

Find a leg: subtract the squares

Square the hypotenuse and the known leg, subtract, then take the square root.

A leg is always shorter than the hypotenuse. If your answer is longer, you added instead of subtracting.

Pythagorean triples

Some right triangles have three whole-number sides. Multiples of a triple are triples too (6, 8, 10).

LegsHypotenuseCheck
3 and 459 + 16 = 25
5 and 121325 + 144 = 169
8 and 151764 + 225 = 289
7 and 242549 + 576 = 625

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the sides: 3 + 4 = 7Square first: 3² + 4² = 25, so c = 5
Subtracting to find the hypotenuseHypotenuse: add the squares. Leg: subtract
Stopping at c² = 25Take the square root: c = 5
Calling the bottom side the hypotenuseFind the side opposite the right angle
Rounding before the last stepRound only the final square root

faq.q: Is the Pythagorean theorem taught in Grade 8 in Ontario?
faq.a: Yes. In the Grade 8 Ontario math curriculum (Spatial Sense, E2.4), students describe the Pythagorean relationship with geometric models such as squares on the sides, and use it to find an unknown side of a right triangle.

faq.q: How do you know which side is the hypotenuse?
faq.a: The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle, and it is always the longest side. The two sides that form the right angle are the legs.

faq.q: How do you find a missing leg with the Pythagorean theorem?
faq.a: Subtract instead of add: square the hypotenuse and the known leg, subtract, then take the square root. For example, √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12.
Three whole numbers that fit a² + b² = c², such as 3, 4, 5 or 5, 12, 13. Any multiple, like 6, 8, 10, is also a triple.

sets.title: Squares on the sides: the area model

items.q: Squares are drawn on the sides of a right triangle. What is the area of the square marked “?”
items.e: The two squares on the legs add up to the square on the hypotenuse: ? + 25 = 61. So ? = 61 − 25 = 36 m².

items.q: Squares are drawn on the sides of a right triangle. What is the area of the square on the hypotenuse?
items.e: The square on the hypotenuse equals the two smaller squares put together: 40 + 24 = 64 m². (The hypotenuse itself is √64 = 8 m long.)

items.q: A triangle has sides of 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm. Is it a right triangle?
items.e: Square the sides: 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100, and 10² = 100. They match, so it is a right triangle.

items.q: The squares on the legs of a right triangle have areas of 36 m² and 64 m². How long is the hypotenuse?
items.e: The square on the hypotenuse is 36 + 64 = 100 m². Its side is √100 = 10 m.

items.q: Squares are drawn on the sides of a right triangle. What is the area of the square marked “?”

items.q: Squares are drawn on the sides of a right triangle. What is the area of the square on the hypotenuse?
items.e: The square on the hypotenuse equals the two smaller squares put together: 36 + 64 = 100 m². (The hypotenuse itself is √100 = 10 m long.)

items.q: A triangle has sides of 7 cm, 8 cm and 11 cm. Is it a right triangle?
items.e: Square the sides: 7² + 8² = 49 + 64 = 113, but 11² = 121. They do not match, so it is not a right triangle (its largest angle is a little more than 90°).

items.q: Squares are drawn on the sides of a right triangle. What is the area of the square on the hypotenuse?

items.q: Squares are drawn on the sides of a right triangle. What is the area of the square on the hypotenuse?
items.e: The square on the hypotenuse equals the two smaller squares put together: 9 + 16 = 25 cm². (The hypotenuse itself is √25 = 5 cm long.)

items.q: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 17 cm and one leg of 8 cm. What is the area of the square on the other leg?
items.e: Square on the hypotenuse: 17² = 289 cm². Square on the known leg: 8² = 64 cm². Other square: 289 − 64 = 225 cm².

items.q: Squares are drawn on the sides of a right triangle. What is the area of the square on the hypotenuse?
items.e: The square on the hypotenuse equals the two smaller squares put together: 12 + 13 = 25 cm². (The hypotenuse itself is √25 = 5 cm long.)

items.q: Squares are drawn on the sides of a right triangle. What is the area of the square marked “?”
items.e: The two squares on the legs add up to the square on the hypotenuse: ? + 16 = 41. So ? = 41 − 16 = 25 cm².

items.q: Squares are drawn on the sides of a right triangle. What is the area of the square marked “?”
items.e: The two squares on the legs add up to the square on the hypotenuse: ? + 36 = 100. So ? = 100 − 36 = 64 m².

items.q: The square on the hypotenuse of a right triangle has an area of 169 cm². How long is the hypotenuse?
items.e: The side of a square is the square root of its area: √169 = 13 cm, because 13 × 13 = 169.

items.q: Each choice gives the areas of three squares, in cm². Which three squares could be drawn on the sides of a right triangle?
items.e: The two smaller areas must add up to the largest: 20 + 30 = 50. Check the others: 20 + 30 = 50, not 40; 16 + 36 = 52, not 49; 25 + 36 = 61, not 64.

items.q: Each choice gives the areas of three squares, in cm². Which three squares could be drawn on the sides of a right triangle?
items.e: The two smaller areas must add up to the largest: 25 + 144 = 169. Check the others: 25 + 144 = 169, not 196; 5 + 12 = 17, not 13; 16 + 25 = 41, not 36.

items.q: The legs of a right triangle are 5 cm and 12 cm. What is the area of the square on the hypotenuse?
items.e: The squares on the legs are 5² = 25 cm² and 12² = 144 cm². The square on the hypotenuse is 25 + 144 = 169 cm².

items.q: Each choice gives the areas of three squares, in cm². Which three squares could be drawn on the sides of a right triangle?
items.e: The two smaller areas must add up to the largest: 64 + 225 = 289. Check the others: 8 + 15 = 23, not 17; 64 + 225 = 289, not 256; 49 + 64 = 113, not 121.

items.q: Squares are drawn on the sides of a right triangle. What is the area of the square on the hypotenuse?
items.e: The square on the hypotenuse equals the two smaller squares put together: 18 + 31 = 49 cm². (The hypotenuse itself is √49 = 7 cm long.)

items.q: A right triangle has sides of 0.8 m, 1 m and 0.6 m. Which length is the hypotenuse?
c: You cannot tell without a picture.
items.e: The hypotenuse is the longest side of a right triangle: 1 m. Check: 0.6² + 0.8² = 0.36 + 0.64 = 1 = 1².

items.q: A right triangle has sides of 21 cm, 29 cm and 20 cm. Which length is the hypotenuse?
c: You cannot tell without a picture.
items.e: The hypotenuse is the longest side of a right triangle: 29 cm. Check: 20² + 21² = 400 + 441 = 841 = 29².

items.q: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is the side that is …
c: at the bottom of the triangle
items.e: The hypotenuse is across from (opposite) the right angle. The two sides that form the right angle are the legs.

items.q: Which equation is true for this right triangle?
items.e: The hypotenuse is a, the side opposite the right angle. The squares of the two legs add up to the square of the hypotenuse: b² + c² = a². The letters do not matter: here the hypotenuse is called a.

items.q: In which triangle is the red side the hypotenuse?
items.e: The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle (the small square). In triangle C the red side is across from the right angle. In the others the red side touches the right angle, so it is a leg.

items.q: Which statement about the hypotenuse of a right triangle is always true?
c: It equals the two legs added.
It is the side at the bottom.
It is shorter than one leg.
items.e: The hypotenuse is always the longest side, because its square equals the squares of both legs added together. It can be drawn in any direction, and it is shorter than the two legs added together.

sets.title: Word problems: ladders, ramps, parks and screens

items.q: A wheelchair ramp at a community centre rises 0.5 m over a horizontal distance of 6 m. How long is the sloping surface of the ramp? Round to the nearest tenth.
A TV screen is 96 cm wide and 54 cm tall. TV sizes are measured along the diagonal of the screen. How long is the diagonal? Round to the nearest tenth.
A 3 m ramp goes from the back of a moving truck to the ground. The back of the truck is 0.9 m high. How far from the truck does the ramp touch the ground? Round to the nearest tenth.
items.e: d² = 3² − 0.9² = 9 − 0.81 = 8.19. d = √8.19 ≈ 2.86…, which rounds to 2.9 m. The ramp is the hypotenuse.

items.q: Noah hikes 2.4 km east and then 1.8 km north in Algonquin Park. How far is he from the trailhead, in a straight line?
The bases on a baseball diamond form a square with sides of 27.4 m. How far does the catcher throw from home plate straight to second base? Round to the nearest tenth.
items.e: c² = 27.4² + 27.4² = 750.76 + 750.76 = 1501.52. c = √1501.52 ≈ 38.74…, which rounds to 38.7 m. Home plate, first base and second base make a right triangle.

items.q: An older TV has a screen with a 100 cm diagonal. The screen is 80 cm wide. How tall is it?
On a canoe trip, Mei paddles 1.2 km north and then 0.5 km east across a lake. How far is she from the starting point, in a straight line?
Aiden flies a kite on a 50 m string. The kite is right above a point on the ground 30 m away from him. How high is the kite? (Ignore his height.)
items.e: h² = 50² − 30² = 2500 − 900 = 1600. h = √1600 = 40 m. The string is the hypotenuse.

items.q: A window is 6 m above the ground. For safety, the foot of a ladder must be 1.5 m from the wall. How long must the ladder be to reach the window? Round to the nearest tenth.
A square schoolyard is 40 m on each side. How long is a path straight across it from one corner to the opposite corner? Round to the nearest tenth.
A park in Ottawa is a rectangle 120 m long and 50 m wide. A path goes straight across it from one corner to the opposite corner. How long is the path?
A tablet screen is 24 cm wide and 18 cm tall. How long is its diagonal?
An NHL hockey rink is about 61 m long and 26 m wide. About how far is it diagonally from one corner to the opposite corner? Round to the nearest tenth.
Arjun leans a ladder against a wall so that it reaches 3.6 m up the wall. The foot of the ladder is 1.5 m from the wall. How long is the ladder?
items.e: c² = 3.6² + 1.5² = 12.96 + 2.25 = 15.21. c = √15.21 = 3.9 m. The ladder is opposite the right angle between the wall and the ground.

items.q: Amira builds a skateboard ramp that is 0.7 m high and 2.4 m long along the ground. How long is the sloping top of the ramp?
A soccer field is 100 m long and 64 m wide. How far is it from one corner flag to the opposite corner flag, in a straight line? Round to the nearest tenth.
A garden gate is 1.2 m wide and 1 m tall. A wooden brace goes from one corner to the opposite corner. How long is the brace? Round to the nearest tenth.
A wire runs from a point 8 m up a flagpole to a stake in the ground 6 m from the bottom of the pole. How long is the wire?
A 5 m ladder leans against the wall of Priya’s cottage. Its foot is 1.2 m from the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach? Round to the nearest tenth.
items.e: h² = 5² − 1.2² = 25 − 1.44 = 23.56. h = √23.56 ≈ 4.85…, which rounds to 4.9 m. The ladder is the hypotenuse; the ground and the wall are the legs.
